subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Metamaterials: Bending Physics
description: A quick, practical guide to Metamaterials: Bending Physics.

hook.text: Metamaterials can bend light around objects, making them invisible. Not science fiction — lab reality.

buildup.text: Their properties come from structure, not chemistry. Tiny patterns smaller than a wavelength of light change how waves behave.

discovery.text: In 2006, Duke University demonstrated a copper-ring metamaterial that bent microwaves around an object.

twist.text: Acoustic metamaterials can cancel sound. Engineers are developing walls that block noise without adding mass.

climax.text: Seismic metamaterials could protect buildings from earthquakes by redirecting shockwaves around foundations.

punchline.text: Materials that break the rules of nature. By design.

quiz.question: What gives metamaterials their unusual properties?
options: Rare elements that interact with electromagnetic fields
Tiny structural patterns that change how waves behave
Chemical coatings that absorb and redirect energy
